mainEntity.name: How much does a Jaguar XJ 2.7D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Jaguar XJ 2.7D engine typically costs between £1,600 and £2,800 for supply only, while a reconditioned unit ranges from £1,500 to £2,600. Used engines are cheaper (£800-£1,500) but carry unknown history and higher inherent risk. Labour for supply and fit adds approximately £600 to £900 depending on the specialist. All EnginesMarket quotes include a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty coverage.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common problems with the Jaguar XJ 2.7D engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.7L TDV6 (276DT) is generally robust but has two well-documented failure points: cylinder liner sealing washer degradation causing coolant to mix with oil, and plastic oil filter housing cracks leading to sudden oil pressure loss. Turbocharger oil feed pipe blockage is also common if service intervals are extended. Catching these issues early with preventative seal and housing replacement can save the engine. Warning: Ignoring oil pressure warnings or coolant loss can lead to rapid bearing failure and complete engine seizure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Jaguar XJ 2.7D?

acceptedAnswer.text: For an XJ 2.7D valued between £1,500 and £4,000, a full rebuilt engine may approach the vehicle's market value. However, if the chassis, interior, and transmission are in excellent condition, a specialist-fitted rebuilt unit at £1,600-£2,800 can extend the car's life significantly. Evaluate scrap or part-exchange value first if the bodywork is heavily corroded. A high-quality used engine (£800-£1,500) may be a viable short-term solution for budget-conscious owners. Rebuilt units include upgraded seals and housings addressing original failure points.

mainEntity.name: Will a Land Rover 2.7 TDV6 engine fit my Jaguar XJ 2.7D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the 276DT 2.7L TDV6 was shared across the Jaguar XJ, Land Rover Discovery 3, and Range Rover Sport platforms. However, mounting points, ancillary brackets, and ECU calibration differ between applications. The core block architecture is identical across Jaguar and Land Rover models. Engine mounts, wiring looms, and turbo plumbing vary by vehicle application. Using a Jaguar-donor 276TD minimises compatibility risks during replacement fitting.

mainEntity.name: Does a replacement Jaguar XJ 2.7D engine need ECU coding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most Jaguar XJ 2.7D engine swaps do not require full ECU reprogramming if you fit an identical 276DT engine code. However, the PATS immobiliser system may require a dealer-level diagnostic tool to pair the new engine's ECU with your car's existing security module. Matching engine codes usually plug-and-play without complex coding. Supply and fit specialists often handle ECU pairing as part of the installation service.

historyTimeline.h2: Jaguar XJ 2.7D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: Launched in 2005 as the first-ever diesel engine option for the Jaguar XJ, the 2.7D utilised the Ford/PSA-developed 2.7-litre TDV6 (276DT) engine, delivering strong torque and executive refinement before being replaced by the 3.0L unit in the next generation.

milestones.description: 276DT, 2.7L Diesel, 204hp (Introduction of the first diesel engine in the Jaguar XJ lineup, X350 generation)
276DT, 2.7L Diesel, 207hp (Minor power bump and emissions hardware refinements during the X350 facelift)
Production of the 2.7D ceased as the X350 was replaced by the X351 generation, which introduced the 3.0L TDV6.

commonProblems.h2: Jaguar XJ 2.7D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Jaguar XJ 2.7D offers strong torque and executive refinement, but its Ford/PSA-derived 2.7L TDV6 (276DT) engine carries well-documented vulnerabilities, particularly around cooling system leaks and turbocharger oil feed issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded internal components designed to address the original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.group: Cylinder Liner & Oil Filter Housing Leaks
problems.h4: Cylinder Liner & Oil Filter Housing Leaks - Why the Jaguar XJ 2.7D Loses Coolant and Pressure
problems.rootCause: The cylinder liner sealing washers degrade over time, allowing coolant to seep into the sump and dilute the oil. Concurrently, the plastic oil filter housing becomes brittle from heat cycling and can crack, causing sudden and catastrophic oil pressure loss.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing cylinder liner seals, fitting an upgraded metal or reinforced oil filter housing, and flushing the cooling system
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective preventative measure if caught before internal engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt 276DT unit with upgraded seals, reinforced housings, and a 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The only reliable solution if oil starvation or hydrolock has already caused bearing or piston damage

problems.recommendation: If caught early, replacing the oil filter housing and liner seals is a highly cost-effective preventative measure. However, if the engine has suffered oil starvation, metallic knocking, or hydrolock from coolant ingress, a rebuilt 276DT unit with upgraded seals and housings is the only reliable long-term solution.

problems.group: Turbocharger Oil Feed Blockage & Actuator Failure
problems.h4: Turbocharger Oil Feed Blockage & Actuator Failure - Why the Jaguar XJ 2.7D Loses Power
problems.rootCause: Sludge buildup from extended service intervals restricts the narrow turbo oil feed pipe, leading to centre bearing wear. Additionally, the electronic wastegate actuator develops linkage play, triggering limp mode and reduced boost.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Removing the turbo, replacing the core and actuator, and flushing the oil feed lines
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the failure is isolated to the turbocharger and the engine block remains healthy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt engine with a new turbocharger assembly and upgraded oil management components
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if turbo bearing failure has sent metallic debris into the intake or oil galleries
